title: Unit: calls, response status, and crew checks
audience: Apparatus crews and authorized members who manage call information from Unit.
summary: Work the incident lifecycle with the correct unit and crew context, then complete the required check without confusing incident, status, and checklist states.
prerequisites: A selected demo unit, role assignments, configured response statuses, safe dispatch recipients, and a call with location and destination.
Create/edit/close permissions for those optional branches; prepared call extras, timers, video, command, and site data.
Checklists.System enabled with a published checklist and a due or on-demand target.

Preserve Engine51 unit role51001 Officer/TeamLead = Christopher Herrmann only. The other five units remain unassigned; do not change member status, shift assignments or qualifications for this crew example.

scenes.capture_intent: Show actual call-ID/Nature filter and selected call; Clear search uses the actual DOM-named X icon. Number/title queries are not claimed supported. Do not require New Call as literal text for the unnamed plus FAB.
scenes.narration: Open Calls and locate the training incident before opening it. Search uses internal call ID or incident nature. In this exercise, 51009 finds the disposable training call; confirm its displayed number and identifying details before acting. Clear search restores the wider list. Apply the same care to mobile crisis visits, wildland responses, or industrial exercises, where similar descriptions can mislead.
scenes.practice: Find the fictional transport incident assigned to the demo ambulance without creating a duplicate call.

scenes.title: Update unit status with a destination
scenes.capture_intent: Capture source-offered destination/note steps and actual Submit or hold control; verify saved result, and label genuine queue state only if it occurs. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: In Select Status, choose the configured unit state and follow any destination and note steps. Calls, Stations, and POIs appear only when that state supports them. Hold to submit is used in enabled hold mode; ordinary mode uses Submit. A queued message describes local work awaiting transmission. Confirm the later saved state before saying the department received the change, and keep physical movement claims separate.

If the app reports the update is queued, inspect that state and its later synchronization rather than assuming dispatch has already received the new status.

scenes.title: Complete the crew’s checklist deliberately
scenes.capture_intent: Select active-unit checklist; capture required/conditional fields, save/resume/submit only fictional answers, and actual witness boundary without attestation. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: Due checks lets the crew choose an apparatus target and Start checklist. Read the version and required items, record only exercise answers, and explain any Not applicable choice. Save progress and Submit checklist have different outcomes; a witness-required run needs another authenticated reviewer. Photos, signatures, and durable native offline recovery require their own evidence. Checklist completion does not close the call or make the unit available.
scenes.practice: Resume a fictional apparatus check, review a photo and reason, then prepare the checklist for submission or its required witness.

source_workflow_reference.title: Complete the crew’s checklist deliberately
source_workflow_reference.narration: Open Due checks and select the appropriate apparatus or crew target before Start checklist. Answer the required items, add evidence, and explain any Not applicable response with its reason. Save progress keeps a run resumable; Submit checklist moves it into a submitted state. A witness-required run needs a different authenticated reviewer. Keep checklist completion separate from a call closure or a unit becoming available.

scenes.title: Close, deselect, and reset deliberately
scenes.capture_intent: Use a separate approved disposable call for actual closure; keep51002 open and avoid parent-reserved51006. Capture Close form/result, Deselect confirmation/result, and unit status separately. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: Close Call requires the permitted Close Type and a useful Close Note, with any offered notification choices reviewed before submission. Use a separate coordinator-approved exercise for closure. Deselect has its own confirmation and clears the selected incident; unit availability is another status action. Unit uses a browser confirmation for Deselect on web. Verify all resulting states without implying that related records or checklists were finalized.
scenes.practice: Close a disposable exercise, clear its active selection, and review the next valid apparatus status without changing a real response.

source_workflow_reference.title: Close, deselect, and reset deliberately
source_workflow_reference.narration: An authorized user closes the incident with Close Call, the appropriate Close Type, and a useful Close Note. Review the optional notification scope before confirming. Deselect clears the active call selection, while the configured unit-status transition describes whether the apparatus is available for another assignment. Review all three states separately. Closing an exercise should leave a clear outcome without implying that every related record or checklist was finalized.

capture_limitations: No actual Unit scene-to-screen proof is established by this source audit.
No credential/factor/device-security changes or GPS/audio/native permissions are exercised.
Unrendered API/store operations are not app-screen walkthrough actions.
No external ordering/AI/voice provider, notification delivery, physical arrival, durable native offline operation, or financial submission success is claimed.
